⁉️Property Lines, Drawn After Midnight

The Yellow Line doesn't need a treaty. It just needs a bulldozer and a shift after dark.

Overnight, yellow concrete blocks landed on Salah al-Din Street in Shuja'iyya, near the intersection with Mashtaha Street in the Sanafer area, sealing off the main north-south artery that runs from Gaza City to Rafah. 

Palestinian sources reported the barriers going up while residents were asleep — waking up to find their commute annexed. 

This is the same corridor the Israeli military has been squeezing for months, moving the same yellow line that already swallowed 64.9 percent of Gaza's territory as of June, up from 53 percent at the ceasefire's start.

Same night, same script, different neighborhood. In Deir al-Balah, the line pushed west again — this time cutting through land where the Israeli settlement of Kfar Darom once stood, about two kilometers from the Strip's border and one kilometer east of Salah al-Din. 

Field sources have already logged the pattern of 100-to-350-meter westward creeps here, each one quietly bringing more Palestinian homes inside Israeli-held territory without warning or legal grounding under the ceasefire text.

No summit announced this. No spokesman signed anything. A concrete cube just changed address, and with it, so did the map. Call it urban planning, if the planner carries an M4 and works exclusively at night.

The ceasefire calls this line temporary. The bulldozers apparently didn't get the memo — or got a different one.

If a border can move a kilometer without anyone declaring war, was it ever really a border, or just a suggestion with rebar in it?

📜Enoch Scrolls—The Sacred Wait

Sometimes God asks us to wait.

Not because He has forgotten us.
Not because He is withholding His goodness.
Not because He is testing how long we can endure.

He asks us to wait because eternity sees what today cannot.

We are creatures who long for answers. We want to know where the path leads, how the story ends, and when the breakthrough will come. Yet faith has never been about seeing the whole staircase. Faith has always been about taking the next step, trusting the One who already stands at the top.

The world says,
“I’ll believe it when I see it.”

God whispers,
“Believe Me… and then you will see.”

There is a holy mystery in that.

The greatest miracles often begin long before we recognize them. A seed buried beneath the soil appears lifeless, yet beneath the surface roots are quietly reaching into places no eye can see. Heaven often works the same way. While we believe nothing is happening, God is weaving together people, places, circumstances, and hearts with perfect precision.

What feels like silence is often sacred preparation.

Waiting is not wasted time.

It is the workshop where God shapes our character, deepens our faith, softens our hearts, and teaches us that His presence is greater than any promise we seek.

The longer I walk with Him, the more I realize His greatest gift is not always the answer to my prayer.

It is His peace while I wait.

A peace that doesn’t make human sense.

A peace that steadies a trembling heart.
A peace that quiets anxious thoughts.
A peace that whispers, “You don’t have to carry this anymore. I’ve already gone before you.”

When we surrender our timeline, we discover His timing.

When we surrender control, we discover His faithfulness.

When we surrender fear, we discover His perfect love.

That is the paradox of faith.

The more we loosen our grip, the more securely we find ourselves held.

Maybe today you can’t see what God is doing.

Maybe every door seems closed.
Maybe the phone hasn’t rung.
Maybe the relationship hasn’t healed.
Maybe the diagnosis hasn’t changed.
Maybe the provision hasn’t arrived.

But the absence of visible movement is never the absence of God’s hand.

He has never abandoned a promise.

Not once.

His delays are not His denials.

His silence is not His absence.

His waiting room is never empty. It is filled with unseen work that only heaven can accomplish.

One day you will look back and realize the season you thought was holding you back… was actually holding you together.

So today…

Rest.

Not because you know what tomorrow holds.

But because you know the One who holds tomorrow.

Trust Him with the chapters you cannot yet read.

Walk by faith, even when your eyes cannot see.

And discover the beautiful secret that only those who wait upon the Lord ever truly understand:

The miracle is not only what God has prepared for you…

The miracle is the person you become while waiting.

“But those who wait on the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles, they shall run and not be weary, they shall walk and not faint.” — Isaiah 40:31

Reflection:
If you find yourself in a season of waiting today, don’t ask God to hurry the promise. Ask Him to help you become the person He is preparing to receive it.

Prayer

Heavenly Father,

Teach us to trust You in the waiting.

When our hearts grow anxious because we cannot see what You are doing, remind us that You are always working behind the scenes. Help us to remember that silence is not Your absence and delays are not Your denial. Strengthen our faith to believe Your promises even when our eyes cannot yet see them fulfilled.

Lord, quiet the voices of fear, doubt, and uncertainty that so easily steal our peace. Replace them with the confidence that comes from knowing You are a good Father who never leaves His children and never breaks a promise.
